Bug_Details:
In Java, the Object.equals() method is used for object comparison, and it is typically overridden in classes to provide a custom
equality check based on your criteria for equality.
The default implementation of equals() provided by the Object class compares the memory references of the two objects,
that means it checks if the objects are actually the same instance in memory.
The "equals" as a method name should be used exclusively to override Object.equals(Object) to prevent confusion.
It is important to note that when you override equals() , you should also override the hashCode() method to maintain the
contract between equals() and hashCode() .
Bug_Explanation: In the EqualsMethodBug class, the equals method is overridden but it accepts a parameter of type EqualsMethodBug instead of the required Object type. This might result in unexpected behavior when comparing objects of this class with objects of other classes.
Trigger_Explanation: The bug is triggered when the EqualsMethodBug.equals(Object) method is not overridden correctly. In the test case, this happens when the EqualsMethodBug.showBug(EqualsMethodBug) method is called with an argument of type EqualsMethodBug, even though the EqualsMethodBug.equals(Object) method expects an argument of type Object.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results do not demonstrate any errors or exceptions that would be indicative of the bug being triggered. While the equals method does not accept Object parameters, it is not called with an Object input in the test code, so the bug was not triggered.
